reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Read DRAFT, CONTEXT, SOURCE and the_change first; opened ADMISSION.json only after my own pass. CHANGE CHECK: the_change asks for Emulate's three sentences in place of the source's two (what the inherited parent script is; it isn't always a voice; it isn't the inner adult you build), with “This” put back for “It” in the last. The draft is exactly those three sentences in that order, the third opens “This is not the inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Guide) that you consciously build.”, and none of the source's own wording (“internalized”, “build up on purpose”, “not the same as”) is left in CONTEXT, which holds the draft once, unbroken. MEANING vs SOURCE: “the set of rules and ways of treating yourself” becomes “a collection of rules and ways of treating yourself”; “internalized as a child” becomes “adopted as a child”; “mostly based on how your parent(s) treated you” becomes “(mostly based on how you were treated by your parent(s))”; “doesn’t always sound like a voice” becomes “doesn’t always take the form of a voice”; “not the same as your inner adult … that you build up on purpose” becomes “not the inner adult … that you consciously build”. Same points, same order, nothing added or dropped: no first person, no study, no figure, no new fact. “Adopted” for “internalized” is a small register shift, not a meaning shift (the child takes the rules on; the following sentences show the script acting as an imposed critic, so it does not read as free choice), and “adopted” does not clash with “inherited” in the heading (given by the parents, taken on by the child). READS IN CONTEXT: “Your parent script is made up of …” picks up and defines “your inherited parent script” in the sentence before it, so it follows. “It” in the second sentence is the script (subject of the first). “This” in the third is also the script; the nearest noun is “a voice”, but “a voice is not the inner adult” is not something the paragraph could mean and the next sentence goes on with “this script”, so I read it as pointing at the script (the source used the same construction). The following “Often this script acts as a critic or warden, telling …” follows well from “doesn’t always take the form of a voice” (the “often” answers the “not always”). Register is a little more written than the source (“made up of a collection of”, “take the form of”, “consciously”) but matches the neighbouring “One important thing to become aware of … is”. Cosmetic only: the parenthetical ends in nested parentheses “(… parent(s))”, a little clumsy, not a tell. TELL ROWS: went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the draft inside its paragraph; none is PRESENT. Looked hardest at: T02 (definition, then “not always a voice”, then “not the inner adult” are three plain declaratives, but they are followed by a long concrete list of what the script says (“not to cry, not to be “needy” …”) and by the irony of it calling loving talk “fake”, so it is not a run of compressed lessons); T09 (sentence weights are uneven, about 35, 9 and 15 words); T12 and T16 (the contrast of “adopted as a child” with “consciously build” is the distinction the article needs between the script and the inner adult, and there is no “not X, it’s Y” flip because the first sentence already says what the script is); T13 (the “doesn’t always take the form of a voice” qualification is a counterexample arising from the definition, and the paragraph closes on an aside, not a slot filler); T15 (the swaps are to common phrases, “adopted”, “take the form of”, “made up of”, not to less likely words, and the structure is the source's by design of this lane); T21 (the first sentence is one thought: what it is, when, and on what basis, and splitting off the “voice” clause lowers the packing the source had); T22 (no “you can”, “you’ll want”, no reassurance); C01 (the inner child is not called “the kid”); C02 (pronouns checked above); C03 and C04 (nothing claimed that the source does not already say). LINTER FINDINGS: “D9 follows the source order” – accepted: this is a sentence-for-sentence swap inside one paragraph, so it follows the source's points by construction and moves nothing (T14 absent); the T13 and T09 check it asks for comes out as above. “E36/E41 heavy second person” (9.1 per 100) – accepted: the “you”s are the reader's own history and what the reader builds (“that you adopted as a child”, “how you were treated”, “that you consciously build”), the whole guide is addressed to “you”, and nothing here coaches (T22 absent). INDEPENDENCE NOTE: my context also held the repository's standing instruction files, which the harness loads automatically; I saw none of the writer's reasoning beyond ADMISSION.json, which I opened after forming my own rows, and I agree with its rows and its two linter dispositions.
